title: Memory-like innate response to booster vaccination with MF-59 adjuvanted influenza vaccine in children.
ehr_evidence: Blood for transcriptomics, HAI and cellular response was collected at all of the time points indicated in Fig. 1a.
summary: Clinical study comparing transcriptional, cellular, and antibody responses to MF59-adjuvanted trivalent inactivated influenza vaccine in children (15–24 months) and young adults.
key_findings: Post-boost vaccination induced a stronger transcriptional response with 221 significantly regulated genes (FDR < 0.05, fold-change > 1.5) in children.
Adults showed a stronger response with 678 significantly regulated genes.
Seroconversion rates for children were 23/24 for H1N1, 22/24 for H3N2, and 19/24 for B/Phuket.
Seroprotection (HAI ≥ 1:629) was achieved in 6/24 for H1N1, 20/24 for H3N2, and 0/24 for B/Phuket.
Elevated interferon response pathways correlated with early-onset local reactogenicity (erythema/swelling), but no correlates were found for fever.
study_design: Prospective clinical trial with staggered sample collection
population: 90 children aged 15–24 months and 30 healthy young adults aged 25–40 years
limitations: Staggered sample collection design limited blood draw frequency per child.
Cohorts B and C lacked pre-vaccination baseline at day 1 and 3 post boost.
Most innate immunity module correlations with HAI titers did not reach statistical significance.
